PanelRegistry::register() does not reject a duplicate ID in the Filament 3.x source: it assigns into the panels array keyed by $panel->getId(), so a later registration replaces the earlier panel for that key. That is overwrite semantics, with no duplicate-ID exception visible in the implementation. Filament’s own configuration docs describe a panel name as unique, so uniqueness is an application/provider invariant rather than a runtime guard.
HasPlugins::plugins(array $plugins) iterates the submitted plugins and calls plugin() for each; plugin() calls the plugin’s register($panel) before storing it keyed by $plugin->getId(). Consequently, duplicate IDs can cause every submitted instance’s registration side effects, while only the final instance remains retrievable from the keyed collection.
For spatie/laravel-permission, team isolation is caller-managed: enable teams, establish the active team ID (normally middleware), and on a team switch call setPermissionsTeamId() plus unload cached roles/permissions relations. Cache reset is automatic when using package APIs/model events, but direct DB writes, custom non-default models, explicit test/seeder workflows, and stale long-lived-worker scenarios require caller action such as forgetCachedPermissions() or an Octane reset listener.
Uncertainty: this is verified against the linked Filament 3.x branch and current Spatie documentation; behavior may differ across major versions.
